newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. group to build $50 mln brewery in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group to build $50 mln brewery in Egypt.

text.p: Egypt's privatised monopoly brewery will begin producing beer by the year 2000 with the help of Danish firms Carlsberg and Danbrew, the U.S.-based firm which bought a majority in the brewery said on Tuesday.

A representative of the Luxor Group told an extraordinary general meeting of al-Ahram Beverages his group would shortly start work on a 170 million pound ($50 million) brewery in the satellite city of Obour and that it was also looking at setting up more production plants in other areas.
Under the sale contract, the Luxor Group must give back to the state al-Ahram's existing breweries in Alexandria and the Cairo suburb of Giza within five years.

The group is committed to invest 221 million pounds in al-Ahram Beverages and the representative said it would spend the remaining 51 million pounds on improving the firm's distribution network and training its workers.
Brewery giant Carlsberg A/S has confirmed its intention to participate in a brewery project in Egypt in cooperation with a local brewer, but said no deal had yet been signed.

Sources close to al-Ahram Beverages said the deal with Carlsberg is likely to be signed soon after the Luxor Group completes the necessary paperwork with the state, expected to happen by the end of this month.
Luxor Group bought 75 percent or 3.37 million shares of al-Ahram Beverages, also known as Pyramids Breweries, from the government last year in a deal worth 231 million pounds.

The brewery workers own 10 percent and the remaining 15 percent was sold through the Cairo stock exchange. The state had originally offered 20 percent but religious opposition to alcohol hit the sale.
The Luxor Group representative also confirmed the group's intention to transform 70 percent of its holdings in al-Ahram into global depositary receipts to be listed in London.

Mostafa Eid, chairman of the state's Holding Company for Housing, Cinema and Tourism, officially approved the transfer of the firm's ownership from the state to private investors and also named the newly elected board.

Seven members of the Luxor Group are on the board as well as representatives of the employee shareholder association, Misr Insurance, which owns a five percent stake, and Bank of Alexandria, which owns another five percent.
Eid also forecast pre-tax profits of 43.4 million pounds for the period from July 1, 1996 to February 18, 1997. The Egyptian financial year begins on July 1.

He did not give any comparative figures but audited results made available earlier this year said al-Ahram Beverages made net after-tax profits of 42.980 million pounds in the financial year 1995/6, 35.8 percent up on 31.654 million in 1994/5.
